title: Weekly comparisons and body goals
summary: Compare muscle sets across weeks, swipe away body-weight goals with Undo and mark attempted sets more clearly. Paste copied screenshots directly into cardio sets. Skip repeated high-rep warnings for one workout. Exercise filter pills follow your theme and toggle off with another tap. Exercise help icons stay aligned beside trends. Hold briefly before reordering sets. Set notes wrap while typing and after saving. Unticking a set also unticks its exercise; tick the exercise again to complete the remaining sets. Exercise search keeps filters and results together when typing or selecting. See weekly volume while you build a split. Workout reactions show each emoji once and highlight only your selection. Workout errors close with an X. The body trend chart extends to a future goal date with a dotted goal line. Filter exercise progress by machine and optionally map machines to a reference, with a recommended reference, suggested conversions and a live preview, for one comparable trend.
changes: **Sets per muscle:** Arrows step back through the last eight weeks on Home and Training, with the week before shown as an outline and the change beside each muscle.
**Body goals:** Swipe a goal's dotted line left in the check-in history to remove it, with Undo for a few seconds.
**Attempted sets:** Failure is now labelled Attempted, with A replacing F in workouts and training splits. Saved workout history uses the same wording.
**Screenshot paste:** Copy a screenshot and tap Paste screenshot beside Upload screenshot in a cardio set to scan it without saving it to Photos.
**High-rep warnings:** Choose not to show rep warnings again for the current workout. The choice survives workout recovery; high-weight warnings stay on.
**Exercise filters:** Selected pills use your theme colour. Tap the selected muscle again to return to All; Custom toggles independently.
**Exercise list:** Muscle-credit help icons line up beside the trend sparklines, including when exercise names wrap.
**Set reordering:** Hold a set's drag handle for half a second until its blue outline appears, then drag to reorder. Quick taps and scrolling keep sets in place.
**Set notes:** Notes wrap onto new lines while typing and after saving, including long words. Manual line breaks are preserved.
**Exercise completion:** Unticking a set also unticks its exercise. Tick the exercise again to complete its remaining entered sets; blank sets keep it unfinished.
**Exercise picker:** Filters stay above the results without large gaps when searching, selecting exercises or opening and closing the keyboard.

**Split editor:** Editing a split opens a compact full screen led by a Weekly volume chart of the sets each muscle gets per week and your planned cardio, against your weekly goals. Days fold into one-line rows, each exercise has a sets stepper with a ? for its direct and partial set credits, and tapping a muscle shows which days train it.
**Split days:** Split cards list each exercise with a coloured block per planned set instead of every set's reps and weight, with a Muscles button to show what each exercise trains.

**Workout reactions:** Each emoji appears once with its count. Only your reaction has a blue border; before reacting, use the smiley-plus button. Tap your emoji to change or remove it, or a count to see who reacted.
**Workout errors:** Tap the X on the right of a workout error, such as a missing completed set, to close it.
**Goal trend line:** With a future target date, the Body trend chart extends to that date and draws a dotted line from your goal's starting weight to the target.

**Machine weights:** Progress has a chip for each saved machine. Turn on Normalise weights from the settings button; the machine you used most in the last three months is recommended as the reference. Relay suggests each other machine's conversion from your logged weights and reps, and a Within 3% badge shows when it lines up with the reference trend. Adjust it with a slider or a pair of equal weights while a preview chart redraws; All machines ≈ then shows one trend in the reference machine's weights. Logged sets, History and records keep the weights you entered.
